sentences.text:
Mr. Mayur Khandeparkar a/w Mr. Vishal Maheshwari and Ms.
 Kamini Pansare i/by V.M. Legal for the Petitioner  Mr. Kedar Dighe, AGP for the State

Mr. Mehmood Pracha for Respondent No. 6  CORAM : NITIN JAMDAR &
 MILIND N. JADHAV, JJ.
DATE : 5 NOVEMBER 2020.
(Through Video Conferencing)

P.C.: 
1. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
2.
Learned counsel for Respondent No. 6 - Food Safety and Standards Authority of India and learned AGP appearing for Respondent Nos. 1 to 5 seek time to file reply affidavit.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
At their request,
stand over to 8 December 2020.
3. Learned counsel for the Petitioner seeks two ad-interim orders.

First that the time given to the Petitioner under the impugned orders to sell the goods in question and deposit the 1 of 3 25. os wpl 5673-20.doc amount be extended without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the Petitioner, if as the State Authorities carry out the auction or sale, the same may affect the reputation of the Petitioner adversely.

Second that pursuant to the impugned order dated 21 July Gujarat Co-Operative Milk Marketing ... vs Adjudicating Officer/Joint ... on 5 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155508897/
1 2020, Respondents - State Authorities be restrained from taking any further coercive steps.

entities.text: 21 July Gujarat Co-Operative Milk Marketing ... vs Adjudicating Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. As regards the first ad-interim relief is concerned, learned AGP, on instructions, states that since the Petitioner did not take steps to sell the goods in question as per the impugned orders which were passed in July 2020 within a time limit of four weeks specified therein and that the goods are perishable, the State Government has already issued notices and tenders have been received and the auction is to be conducted in this week.
In view of this position, we are not inclined to restrain the State Authorities from going ahead with the auction.

We, however, make it clear that we have not granted the request of the Petitioner only because the State Government has already made advance arrangement to sell the goods in question and therefore, there is no question of this action reflecting adversely on the Petitioner's reputation.
5. As regards the second ad-interim order is concerned, it is in respect of a notice of inquiry.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner states that though it is styled as 'Notice of First Inquiry', it is a notice as to why an earlier order should not be implemented.
This notice is of August 2020.
So far no coercive action has been taken against the Petitioner.
Since the petition is being adjourned at the 2 of 3 25.

os wpl 5673-20.doc request of the Respondents for filing replies, we direct that in case the Respondents Authorities intend to take any coercive steps against the Petitioner, they will give 15 days advance notice to the Petitioner.
In that eventuality, liberty to the Petitioner to apply for suitable interim orders in this petition.

6. Needless to state that any amount recovered through the sale conducted by the State Government will be subject to the further orders to be passed in this petition.
7.
This order will be digitally signed by the Private Secretary of this Court.
All concerned to act on production by fax or email of a digitally signed copy of this order.

[ MILIND N. JADHAV, J. ] [ NITIN JAMDAR, J. ]
